facts.value: Feral horses are born and live in the wild, but are descended from domesticated animals.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Many populations of feral horses exist throughout the world.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Studies of feral herds have provided useful insights into the behavior of prehistoric horses, as well as greater understanding of the instincts and behaviors that drive horses that live in domesticated conditions.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Semi-feral horses are privately owned but live for significant amounts of time in 'wild' conditions on undeveloped, often public, lands.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Examples of locations with semi-feral horses include Dartmoor and the New Forest in the UK.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Owners of semi-feral horses often pay a fee for grazing rights.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick
